notes: UNITS: the existing draft wrote 'мм' in Cyrillic throughout. Per the terminology rule I restored Latin 'mm' in lblSizeSel, offXAria, offYAria, calcFmt, shiftedFmt, sizeFmt, sizeFull. 'pt' was already correct in lblSize.

{lbl} SURVIVES IN ALL 12 STRINGS — no string had to drop it. The trick: Mongolian allows an unmarked (indefinite) direct object after a numeral, so '{n} {lbl} дугаарлалаа' is grammatical, and where a case would otherwise be needed I used the postpositions 'дээр' / 'дээрх', which take the nominative: tSet '{n} {lbl} дээр бичлээ', tEmptied '{n} {lbl} дээрх текстийг арилгалаа', tImgPlaced/tTagged '{n} {lbl} дээр …', tUntagged/tRestyled '{n} {lbl} дээрх тэмдгийг …'. Restructured relative to the English word order (Mongolian is verb-final) but nothing was dropped.

RESTRUCTURED word order (English -> Mongolian, all verb-final): tFilled 'Filled {n} labels from {k} lines' -> '{k} мөрөөр {n} {lbl} бөглөлөө' ({k} now leads); tTagCount '{n} labels tagged {c}' -> '{c} тэмдэгтэй {n} {lbl} сонголоо' ({c} now leads, and I made it a sentence because the toast fires when the labels are actually selected); calcFmt puts 'Нэг шошго' in front of {w}/{h} and adds the counter word 'ширхэг' after {n}, which Mongolian needs; shiftedFmt leads with the direction words.

CODE ISSUE 1 (taggedW, worth a one-line dev fix): index.html line ~1081 builds the cell aria-label as t('taggedW') + ' ' + cname(base), producing 'тэмдэгтэй Улаан'. The same word is used in the selection counter as count + ' ' + taggedW ('2 тэмдэгтэй'), which is correct. I optimised for the visible counter. Swapping that one concatenation to cname(base) + ' ' + t('taggedW') for MN would give the perfect 'Улаан тэмдэгтэй' and costs nothing in English.

CODE ISSUE 2 (ofLabel): the markup is fixed as [lblImgSize] — [55%] [ofLabel], i.e. 'Image size — 55% of the label'. Mongolian puts the possessor first ('шошгоны 55%'), so that order cannot be made to read naturally. I used a parenthetical gloss — 'Зургийн хэмжээ — 55% (шошгоны хэмжээнээс)' — which is grammatical and idiomatic in a slider label. If the dev is willing to move the ofLabel span in front of the percentage for MN, the better string is 'шошгоны' giving 'Зургийн хэмжээ — шошгоны 55%'.

BUTTON FITS: sidebar is 340px with 12px padding, so a .g2 button is ~155px (text budget ~19 Cyrillic chars at 13.5px) and a .g3 .btn.sm button is only ~101px (~12 chars), and .btn has white-space:nowrap. Nothing exceeds 22 chars. The three tightest: 'Жагсаалтаар бөглөх' (18, .g2 — fine), 'Жижигрүүлэх' (11 in a .g3 sm slot, ~75px of ~83px — fits but is the tightest in the file), and 'Будах горим асаалттай' (21, but that button is .wide/full-width so it is safe).

SHORTENED FOR FIT: emptySheet was 'Хуудас хоослох' (14 chars) in the draft, which overflows its 101px .g3 cell next to Экспорт/Импорт. Shortened to 'Хоослох' — the section is already titled 'Хуудас' and the confirm dialog spells out what will be emptied.

TERMINOLOGY COLLISION FIXED: the draft used 'Багасгах' for both zoomOut and the type 'Shrink' control. Kept 'Багасгах' for zoom out (tooltip on the − button), 'Багтаах' for zoom-to-fit, and moved Shrink to 'Жижигрүүлэх'. typeHint was rewritten to match.

COLOUR NAME CHANGED: teal (#0f9b8e) was 'Ногоон цэнхэр'; the ordinary Mongolian term is 'Хөх ногоон'. Note that blue (#3b82f6) correctly stays 'Цэнхэр' rather than 'Хөх' because of the light, bright hue. Amber/Orange keep the standard Шар / Улбар шар split. The colour names are lowercased by cname().toLowerCase() in tTagged/tTagCount/tNoTag/tPaintOn — all of them lowercase cleanly in Cyrillic, including the two-word 'хөх ногоон'.

LOANWORDS KEPT DELIBERATELY (beyond the mandated Latin list) because they are what people actually say, not Russianisms with a live Mongolian equivalent: Экспорт/Импорт, Градиент, Курсор, Принтер, Фонт, Текст, Лого, Файл, Хөтөч (native), Масштаб (in printHint, because Chrome's print dialog literally says 'Scale' and Mongolian users say масштаб).

PRINT DIALOG NAMES LEFT IN ENGLISH inside printHint: 'None', 'fit to page', 'Background graphics'. Chrome's print dialog is almost always English on these machines, so the user must match the words on screen. I used « » for the quoted option instead of the source's “ ” — those are the Mongolian quotation marks and both are valid HTML entities in an innerHTML string.
langTitle intentionally remains 'Switch to English' — it is the tooltip shown while the app is already in Mongolian, so it must be readable to someone who wants English.

'Preset' has no good Mongolian loanword; I rendered the whole concept as 'хэмжээ' (savePreset 'Хэмжээг хадгалах', delPreset 'Хэмжээг устгах', tSaved, tDeleted, tBuiltin 'Бэлэн хэмжээ', pPresetName). This matches what the dropdown actually lists — label sizes — and reads naturally.

AMBIGUITY FLAGGED — tLeftover: the English ' — {n} left over' is appended to tFilled and {n} counts leftover LINES, not labels. I made that explicit: ' — {n} мөр үлдлээ'. If the intent was leftover labels, change 'мөр' to 'шошго'.

AMBIGUITY FLAGGED — chipNone: 'None' is a deselect-all action, not a filter. 'Цуцлах' (cancel the selection) is what a Mongolian speaker reads it as; 'Сонголт цуцлах' would be clearer but does not fit the 23px chip row alongside five others.

REGISTER: no '-на уу' on any control label. It appears only in pPresetName (a browser prompt, where it is expected) and in a few first-time hints, where I used the friendly '-аарай/-оорой' form (сонгоорой, аваарай, буулгаарай, нэмээрэй) rather than the bureaucratic '-на уу' the draft used on almost every toast.
tImgAdded quotes the placeImg button label «Сонгосонд тавих» — if that button string is ever changed, update this toast to match.
